narration.text: [softly] If a wall in your house looks like this on a thermal camera, [short pause] don't knock. [long pause] I inspect houses. The camera shows me what walls are hiding. Leaks. Wiring. Mice. [long pause] Last month, a house that had been empty for a year. Power off. Heating off. Cold as a fridge. [long pause] Upstairs, the hallway ends in a blank wall. On the plans, there's nothing behind it. [long pause] [softly] On my camera, there's a warm rectangle. Room sized. Thirty seven degrees. [long pause] Outside, I measure. Two metres of house you can't reach from inside. [long pause] I knock on the wall. [long pause] [whispers] Something knocks back. [short pause] Twice. [long pause] [softly] I write it up as possible water damage. I don't tell the buyers. [long pause] They moved in on Friday. This morning, they sent me a photo. [long pause] They want to know why the wall is warm to the touch. [long pause] [whispers] And why there's a door in it now.
